cards.front: What distinguishes a vector from a scalar?
cards.back: A vector has both magnitude and direction and adds by the triangle law; a scalar has magnitude only.

cards.front: Write the dot product of A and B.
cards.back: A · B = AB cos θ — a scalar.

cards.front: Write the cross product of A and B.
cards.back: A × B = AB sin θ n̂ — a vector normal to both.
cards.note: Direction follows the right-hand rule, so A × B = −(B × A).

cards.front: What is the magnitude of the resultant of two vectors P and Q at angle θ?
When are two non-zero vectors perpendicular?
cards.back: When their dot product is zero.

cards.front: When are two non-zero vectors parallel?
cards.back: When their cross product is the null vector.

cards.front: How do you find the unit vector along A?
cards.back: Â = A / |A| — divide the vector by its own magnitude.

cards.front: What is the magnitude of a vector with components (3, 4, 12)?
What does the scalar triple product A · (B × C) represent geometrically?
cards.back: The volume of the parallelepiped formed by the three vectors. It is zero when they are coplanar.

cards.front: Is work a scalar or a vector, and why?
cards.back: A scalar — it is the dot product of force and displacement, W = F · d.
